evaluations.name: positive_incident_detection
evaluations.input_prompt: Pods in gke-skills-sandbox cannot receive ingress traffic. Inspect active NetworkPolicies and GKE Dataplane V2 configuration.
expected_tools: kubectl get netpol -n gke-skills-sandbox deny-ingress-netpol -o wide

expected_findings.root_cause: Default-deny ingress policy matches target pods and silently drops inbound TCP traffic at eBPF layer.
expected_findings.remediation: Synthesize declarative NetworkPolicy ingress allow rules targeting specific client pod labels and ports.

passing_criteria: Must identify default-deny Ingress policy specification
Must verify cluster Dataplane V2 / Cilium datapath provider
Must generate declarative NetworkPolicy allow rule matching client workload

evaluations.name: complex_edge_case_and_handoff
evaluations.input_prompt: Application pods fail with 'Could not resolve host' after applying strict Egress NetworkPolicy. Diagnose DNS block.

expected_findings.correlation: Differentiates application backend connectivity drops from DNS egress port 53 filtering.
expected_findings.decision: Identifies that egress policy omits allow rule for `kube-dns` on port 53 (UDP/TCP); synthesizes DNS egress rule.

passing_criteria: Must inspect egress rule array for port 53 UDP/TCP allow
Must correlate DNS lookup timeouts with missing egress rule
Must formulate exact NetworkPolicy patch adding kube-dns egress

evaluations.name: benign_condition_guardrail
evaluations.input_prompt: NetworkPolicy web-allow-80 permits ingress from app=frontend on port 80. Are packets dropped?

expected_findings.behavior: Observes explicit ingress allow rule matching client pod selector on port 80. Confirms valid policy; zero actions.

passing_criteria: Must verify ingress rule matches client selector and target port
